Scout out of Desert

AlgorithmsSequences

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Clear every scout out of the sandy desert strip at the top of the board.
How to play: Press a scout, then an empty cell two steps away (over another empty cell). A new scout appears in the middle.

Top rows = desert · bottom rows = land

Look for the math

This is the reverse of peg solitaire jumping, used the way Leibniz liked: run the movie backwards to get scouts out of the desert.

A jump that creates a scout

In ordinary jumping you leap over a neighbour onto empty land and remove the neighbour. Here the mid cell must be empty too: after the leap a scout appears there. So each move increases the number of scouts by one, while shifting one scout two steps.

Clearing the desert strip

Rows above the Level line are desert; the rest is habitable land. You win when every desert cell is empty — scouts may remain on land. The logic test finds a three-move solution on a 4×5 board, so the goal is reachable.

Why reverse helps

The sibling puzzle “Sending Scouts into the Desert” asks how far a party can push into the sand with limited supplies; its answers involve Fibonacci numbers. Working backwards from a cleared desert turns a hard placement question into a sequence of reverse jumps you can try by hand.

Set X=4, Y=3, Level=2 and try to clear the desert in three jumps. Take Back if a branch goes wrong.
